官岭，古道上的孤独守望者

官岭古道

官岭，横樟岭，钓鱼岭，八索岭，午岭，燕田岭，一条条古道从松阳的古镇、古村延伸出去，那些由卵石、块石、青石条砌成的古道，或曲折，或细长，或宽阔，或陡峭，或平缓，或翻山，或越岭，如同藤条一样蜿蜒在田间地头，盘旋在高山峡谷，消失在深山老林间，它们编织出了松阳的交通命脉。松阳至今还保留着几条完整的古道，官岭就是其中一条。

官岭来源有几种说法，据《松阳县地名志》记载：最初村里有人做过官，村边有山岭，故名官岭。另一种说法，官岭是当官人走的道路，即官道或者驿道。也许两种说法兼而有之，历史有时候就是这样，一个很清晰的地名掺杂了多种的传说，反而变得似是而非。古时候进出松阳有五条通道，往北通遂昌，向西通宣平，朝东通丽水、云和，朝南通向龙泉。作为松阳县通往龙泉县交通要道中的一段古道，官岭保存得比较完整，长15里，路宽1到2米，大部分由鹅卵石和块石砌成。千百年来，小径上曾经走过衮衮大员和各式官员，走过挑着农作物的农夫，走过精于算计的商人，也走过清瘦的书生……小径仿佛被风吹向远方，不受羁绊地飞向山体的褶皱，一直飘向更加遥远的福建。

公路修通之后，古道渐渐地没落，一些古道完全被湮没了，从繁华过后回归到了孤寂。官岭和一些残存的古道还坚强地挺立着，它们组成了松阳的沧桑名词。与其他古道不一样的是，官岭古道上矗立着一个千姿百态的传统村落——官岭村，更像是古道上的一个孤独的守望者，成为这条古道上访古探幽的最佳去处。

水口古树林

官岭水口两侧山峦上长满了参天古木，远远望去，分明是群山的镜子，将所有的绿映照其中；近看，如同一块天然的巨大圭璧，将身后的官岭村遮掩得严严实实。

松阳作为1800年的古老县份，古树名木自然能够体现出它古老的一面。松阳境内的古树又以官岭村最具特色，村落四周黑压压地长满了樟树、红枫、香榧、柳杉、红豆杉、毛栗等各色树木，更多的是大片大片的竹林，风吹过，青翠的竹林左右晃动，节奏和韵律的一致性，让人产生一种错觉，仿佛山体跟着清风摇动起婀娜的身姿。此时正值初冬时节，枫树红透了，一团一团的红色连接成片状，呈现出霜叶红于二月花的盛景，的确让人深深地陶醉。

走进树林，随着林木越来越密集，光线渐渐地变得有些昏暗，远处丛林景致变得模糊，画面也变得虚幻，仿佛行走在水底，或者迷失在了深不可测的空间之中。林间充次着各种声响，风沙沙地响着，雨淅淅沥沥地落着，鸟类唧唧喳喳地叫着，虫子啾啾鸣着，各种自然界的声响组成一部交响乐。我向同行的官岭村支部书记陈火盛一打听，官岭村现存古树就有162株，其他树木多不胜数，官岭村是松阳县境内古树最多的村落。加上水口两侧山脉的延续，官岭村的水口密布参天大树，这样的规模放眼整个浙西南也非常罕见，水口文化正是官岭村最大的价值体现。

官岭村严格按照古代的风水学进行布局。水口是古村落非常讲究是一个区域，是村落溪流的出入口，它体现了村落的风水观念，古人在水口处种植大片茂密的树木，他们倍加珍惜水口树木，视之如生命，并代代相沿。官岭村的水口树能够如此大规模地保存下来的确是个奇迹，说明了官岭人受到了良好的宗族教化，坚信风水能够惠及子孙后代，也深深地懂得人与自然和谐相处的道理。山林和水是人生活中不可或缺的重要环节，天地人交织形成的互动气场，促进个人的修行，形成健康的心理。林泉之处，山水可以明目，可以净化空气，良好的环境则能使人生理健康。依山砍柴方便，靠水取水便捷，便利原则可以使生活更加协调。官岭村与山水自然地融合在一起，体现出天人合一的至高境界。

官岭村负氧离子特别高，空气特别纯净，水质特别清澈，整个谷地浮着一层温润的湿度，所以官岭村长寿老人特别多。在村口，我遇见苏根女老奶奶，她刚刚从观音庙上香回来，老人的眼睛闪着水亮亮的光泽，仿佛山林中任意恣肆的绿流淌到了她的眸子之中。一问居然90高寿。我们和她告别的时候，老人握着我的手，那双手粗糙而又干瘪，她说：别嫌弃老人手脏，我活了那么大年纪，可以送给你健康平安。

听她这么一说，一行人纷纷上前和她握手，就这么一个简单的老人，留给了我们很多的思考，简单的生活，简单的追求，以一颗平常心看淡生活，她表现出的是一个普通官岭人的处世观，她平淡无奇的人生摆放在官岭的山水画卷中也变得绮丽起来。

阶梯式村落

一条逶迤而来的溪流将官岭村剖成两半，溪流上布满了累累怪石和绿滋滋的水草，村北一条白练似的山涧从山梁的褶皱处飞流而下，聚成一汪碧绿如翡翠一般的深潭，当地人称溪流为苦马溪、瀑布为苦马瀑、潭水为苦马潭。两条弯曲的小涧从山顶往下流淌，穿越整座村落，潺潺的水流声在村落中响起，使得沉寂的村落充满了生机。

走进村落，一座廊桥和一座石拱桥横跨在溪流上，如同抱拳相迎的主人，笑吟吟地恭立面前。村头村尾各有三座八字撑的石板桥，以及后造的水泥桥将村落连成一个整体。官岭村以它独特的格局迎接每一个来客，我一下子就喜欢上了这个遮蔽在大山深处的古村落。

西侧的村落三三两两的建筑隐匿在竹林中，显得相当的安逸，烘托出山野人家的田园情趣。东侧村落坐落在一处坡面上，200余幢老屋，绝大部分是高低错落的泥墙建筑，夹杂着少量的木头墙壁板房，清一色的小青瓦阴阳合铺覆顶，它们搭积木一般，沿着缓坡层层向上，最大幅度地展现出了村落的面积。远远看去，如同一支整整齐齐的方队，披着乌黑的盔甲，排列成一个巨大的方阵，仿佛随着一声令下，这支队伍便会以排山倒海的阵势俯冲而来。

假如说杨家堂村是一幅油画、界首村是一幅水墨画、黄上村是一幅版画，那么官岭村就是一张素描。官岭村一排排建筑层层向上拔高，后面房屋的泥墙略高出前面房屋的泥墙，后面房屋的屋面也略高出前面房屋的屋面，房屋一层层沿着缓坡向上爬伸。灰色的泥墙带正好处在黑色檐瓦带之间，黑色檐瓦又夹在灰色的泥墙中间，一条一条，一层一层，两种颜色平齐，伸展，交叉，过度，和美地搭配在一起。块状，条状，线状，各种线条有机地组合在一起，在山坡上拉开了一个空前开阔的横截面，村落就以这样威武的姿态展现在天地之间，给人以强悍的视觉冲击，倍感先人奇伟的创造力。这完全是一件艺术品，让人怀疑出自黄宾虹之手。

清代建筑严格按等级规定：庑殿顶等级最高，用于佛殿、皇宫和孔庙等主要的建筑，象征无上的尊贵；歇山顶次之，用于宫殿、园林、坛庙式建筑和其他重要建筑；六品以下官吏及平民住宅的正堂只能用悬山顶或硬山顶，因此官岭村大部分建筑采用悬山顶或硬山顶。令人称奇的是，在众多的悬山顶和硬山顶建筑之外，我还意外地看到了多幢庑殿顶和歇山顶建筑，一个只有不到千人的村落，却聚集了中国传统的四种屋顶建筑模式，这让我困惑，难道是官岭村出过等级非常高的门阀世家吗？一问并非如此。这些建筑多为民居，也就是说，它们是在中国封建等级制度瓦解之后兴建的。风格众多的坡顶格局让我欣赏到了别具一格的建筑美感，这在其他村落中非常罕见，让我臣服于它独特的魅力。

在村落中有板房、吊脚楼、谷仓等众多的木头建筑，村落又多是防

Guanling: The Lonely Watcher on the Ancient Road

Guanling Ancient Road

Guanling, Hengzhangling, Diaoyuling, Basuoling, Wuling, Yantianling — ancient roads extend one after another from the ancient towns and villages of Songyang. These ancient roads, paved with cobblestones, block stones, and bluestone strips, are winding, slender, broad, steep, gentle, crossing mountains and ridges, like vines snaking through fields and farmland, spiraling in high mountain gorges, disappearing into deep forests. They weave the transportation lifeline of Songyang. Songyang still preserves several complete ancient roads today, and Guanling is one of them.

There are several theories about the origin of Guanling. According to the Songyang County Place Names Gazetteer: originally someone in the village served as an official, and there was a mountain ridge beside the village, hence the name Guanling (Official Ridge). Another theory says Guanling was a road traveled by officials, i.e., an official road or post road. Perhaps both theories are partly true. History is sometimes like this — a clear place name mixed with multiple legends becomes ambiguous instead. In ancient times, there were five passages in and out of Songyang: north to Suichang, west to Xuanping, east to Lishui and Yunhe, south to Longquan. As a section of the ancient road on the transportation route from Songyang County to Longquan County, Guanling is relatively well preserved, 15 li long, 1 to 2 meters wide, mostly paved with cobblestones and block stones. For thousands of years, the path has seen numerous high officials and various officials, farmers carrying crops, shrewd merchants, and thin scholars... The path seems blown toward the distance by wind, unconstrainedly flying into the folds of the mountains, drifting all the way to the more distant Fujian.

After highways were built, ancient roads gradually declined, some completely湮没, returning from prosperity to solitude. Guanling and some remaining ancient roads still stand tenaciously, forming the vicissitudes vocabulary of Songyang. Unlike other ancient roads, on the Guanling ancient road stands a traditional village of a thousand postures — Guanling Village, more like a lonely watcher on the ancient road, becoming the best place for exploring antiquity on this road.

Water Mouth Ancient Forest

The mountains on both sides of Guanling's water mouth are covered with towering ancient trees. From afar, they are clearly mirrors of the mountains, reflecting all the green within; up close, they are like a natural giant jade tablet, completely concealing the Guanling Village behind.

As an ancient county of 1,800 years, Songyang's ancient and famous trees naturally reflect its ancient side. Among Songyang's ancient trees, those of Guanling Village are the most distinctive. Around the village, dark and dense camphor trees, red maples, Chinese torreya, Japanese cedar, Chinese yew, and chestnut trees of various colors grow, with more being large bamboo forests. When the wind blows, the green bamboo sways left and right with rhythmic consistency, creating an illusion as if the mountain itself is dancing gracefully with the breeze. It was early winter, and the maple trees were fully red, with clusters of red connecting into patches, presenting the scene of frosted leaves redder than February flowers, truly intoxicating.

Entering the forest, as the trees grew denser, the light gradually dimmed, the distant forest scenery became blurred, and the画面 became虚幻, as if walking underwater or lost in an unfathomable space. The forest was filled with various sounds: wind rustling, rain pattering, birds chirping, insects singing — all natural sounds组成 a symphony. I asked Chen Huosheng, the village party secretary traveling with me, and learned that Guanling Village has 162 surviving ancient trees, with countless other trees. Guanling Village is the village with the most ancient trees in Songyang County.加上 the continuation of the mountains on both sides of the water mouth, the water mouth of Guanling Village is densely covered with towering trees. Such a scale is very rare even throughout southwestern Zhejiang, and water mouth culture is precisely the greatest value embodiment of Guanling Village.

Guanling Village is laid out strictly according to ancient feng shui. The water mouth is an area that ancient villages paid great attention to, the entrance and exit of the village stream, embodying the village's feng shui concept. Ancient people planted large dense forests at the water mouth, cherishing water mouth trees as if they were life, passing this down through generations. That Guanling Village's water mouth trees could be preserved on such a large scale is indeed a miracle,说明 that Guanling people received good clan education, firmly believing that feng shui can benefit future generations, and deeply understanding the principle of harmonious coexistence between humans and nature. Mountains, forests, and water are indispensable important links in human life. The interactive energy field formed by the interweaving of heaven, earth, and humans promotes personal cultivation and forms a healthy psychology. In places of forests and springs, mountains and waters can brighten the eyes and purify the air, and a good environment can make people physically healthy. Cutting firewood by the mountain is convenient, drawing water by the water is convenient, and the convenience principle makes life more coordinated. Guanling Village naturally integrates with mountains and waters, embodying the supreme realm of the unity of heaven and humanity.

Guanling Village has particularly high negative oxygen ions, especially pure air, especially clear water quality, and the entire valley floats with a warm humidity, so Guanling Village has particularly many long-lived elderly people. At the village entrance, I met old lady Su Gennü, who had just returned from burning incense at Guanyin Temple. The old lady's eyes shone with a watery luster, as if the unrestrained green of the mountain forest had flowed into her pupils. Upon asking, she was actually 90 years old. When we said goodbye to her, the old lady held my hand — those hands were rough and shriveled. She said: Don't dislike the old lady's dirty hands; I have lived so many years, I can give you health and peace.

Hearing this, our group stepped forward one after another to shake her hand. Such a simple old lady left us with much to think about — simple life, simple pursuits, viewing life with an ordinary heart. What she showed was the worldview of an ordinary Guanling person, and her unremarkable life, placed in the landscape painting of Guanling, also became beautiful.

Ladder-Type Village

A winding stream cuts Guanling Village in half. The stream is covered with numerous strange rocks and green aquatic plants. North of the village, a white ribbon-like mountain stream plunges down from the folds of the mountain ridge, gathering into a deep pool as green as jade. Locals call the stream Kuma Stream, the waterfall Kuma Waterfall, and the pool Kuma Pool. Two winding small streams flow down from the mountaintop, crossing the entire village, with the gurgling sound of water echoing in the village, filling the quiet village with vitality.

Entering the village, a covered bridge and a stone arch bridge span the stream, like a host greeting with folded fists, standing smiling before us. At the village head and tail, there are three stone slab bridges with splayed supports each, plus later-built concrete bridges connecting the village into a whole. Guanling Village greets every visitor with its unique layout, and I immediately fell in love with this ancient village hidden deep in the mountains.

The buildings on the west side of the village, in twos and threes, are concealed in the bamboo forest, appearing quite peaceful, setting off the pastoral charm of mountain households. The east side of the village sits on a slope, with over 200 old houses, most being高低错落 mud-wall buildings, mixed with a few wooden wall plank houses, all covered with uniform small gray tiles in yin-yang overlapping pattern. They are like building blocks, layer upon layer upward along the gentle slope, maximizing the village's area. From afar, they look like a neat square formation, wearing black armor, arranged into a giant方阵, as if at a command, this队伍 would dive down with an overwhelming momentum.

If Yangjiatang Village is an oil painting, Jieshou Village is an ink painting, and Huangshang Village is a print, then Guanling Village is a sketch. In Guanling Village, rows of buildings rise layer by layer; the mud walls of the rear houses are slightly higher than those of the front houses, and the roofs of the rear houses are also slightly higher than those of the front houses, with houses climbing upward layer by layer along the gentle slope. The gray mud wall bands are exactly between the black eave tile bands, and the black eave tiles are夹 between the gray mud walls — one strip, one layer, the two colors level, extending, crossing, transitioning, beautifully matched together. Block-shaped, strip-shaped, line-shaped, various lines organically combined, opening up an unprecedented broad cross-section on the hillside. The village presents itself between heaven and earth in such a majestic posture, giving a powerful visual impact, making one deeply feel the ancestors' extraordinary creativity. This is completely a work of art, making one suspect it came from the hand of Huang Binhong.

Qing dynasty architecture strictly followed等级 regulations: hip-and-gable roof (wudian) had the highest等级, used for Buddhist halls, imperial palaces, and Confucian temples, symbolizing supreme dignity; gable-and-hip roof (xieshan) was next, used for palaces, gardens, altar-temple buildings and other important buildings; officials below the sixth rank and commoners' main residences could only use overhanging gable roof (xuanshan) or flush gable roof (yingshan), so most Guanling buildings use xuanshan or yingshan roofs. Surprisingly, among the many xuanshan and yingshan buildings, I also意外 saw multiple wudian and xieshan buildings. A village with less than a thousand people actually gathered four traditional Chinese roof types, which puzzled me — did Guanling Village produce a very high-ranking noble family? Upon asking, this was not the case. These buildings were mostly residences, meaning they were built after the collapse of China's feudal等级 system. The diverse sloped roof patterns let me appreciate a unique architectural beauty, very rare in other villages, making me submit to its unique charm.

In the village, there are numerous wooden buildings such as plank houses, stilt houses, and granaries, and the village is mostly built for defense...

sections.content_zh:
山下阳，一幅密布玄机的星象图

一提及风水村落，我们自然而然就跳出了神奇、隐秘、玄妙、迷阵等词汇，位于松阳县城西北方向10公里处的山下阳村就是这样一个机关重重的古村落。它遮蔽在松阴溪流域众多的传统村落中，不显眼，不张扬，不气派，不奢华，村落与自然山水密切地契合着，处处蕴涵着天人合一哲学思想，成为古人理想状态之下人居环境的经典之作。

一走进山下阳村，飘来了一股古典的神秘气息，让人陡生回归故园的感觉。村落中老宅鳞次栉比，巷弄曲曲折折，悬浮着一派盎然的古意，是一幅被现代文明遗落的历史画卷，让人在喧嚣之外感受到了一份恬静与自然。置身期间，只有细心观察，才能琢磨出她的内涵和独特的魅力。

山下阳村表面呈成长方形布局，与一般的传统村落大同小异，然而整座村落隐藏着无限玄机，制造出一个巨大的历史谜团。层出不穷的巷道将村落分割成若干个口字建筑群，高大巍峨的马头墙使得巷道仄而幽深，一座座建筑被分割成一个个独立而连接的空间，宛如八卦迷宫一般。几十条密布的鹅卵石巷弄像村落的脉络，深入浅出，纵横交错。卵石经过筛选，大小基本一致，日久天长，生硬冰冷的卵石被脚步磨砺得失去了锐气，路面泛着藏青光泽。村中道路鲜有十字路口，只有数不清的丁字路口，寓意着子孙世代人丁兴旺。一条巷弄一转折，往往是一幢老宅的后门，或者是一垛隔扇墙。走过几个转角，又见一条通道，仿佛步入迷魂阵。这些巷门起着防盗、防火的作用，巷门一闭就将村落隔离成一块块独立的小天地，人为地制造出割裂的空间。

山下阳村最惊艳的建筑是月池。月池为村落注入了无限灵气，池水中落着粉墙黛瓦的倒影，明明晃晃地将水乡风韵悉数坦落。几只鸭子跳进池塘，嘎嘎地叫唤着，拨开粼粼波光，将一池粉墙黛瓦捣碎。月池是村落的地标，也是村落风水布局的核心建筑之一。月池呈半圆形横卧在村前，设计者通过月亏即赢的风水轮回道理，寄托着对后世的殷切期待。风水墙将月池严严实实地包围着，阻挡着村落风水外流。月池终年不干涸，由环绕村落的水系来维持池塘的丰沛。池后凿有一口水井，历经数百年依旧清冽无比。据村人介绍，井底有一眼活泉水，泉水汩汩上涌，保持了井水的饱满。令人称奇的是，井水和池水咫尺之隔，井水高度却超出池水高度20厘米。一个光着膀子的男人从老井里哗哗地吊上一桶新鲜的水，拎着水桶走进了一扇虚掩的门。这口看似普通的水井，正是古村的眼睛，它见证了山下阳村三百年来的兴衰。

紧挨着月池的是正方形地坛，石砌的堤岸将月池和地坛一分为二，它们形成一组对应的平面建筑，取意天圆地方。地坛是公共活动中心，它是当年用于祭祀天地、迎仕、庆典和公共聚会的场所。月池和地坛展现了山下阳先人对天地的敬畏之情，他们在这里生动地模拟出了天人合一的至高理想，我们站在这里可以深切地感受到天地人三者合一的境界。

距离月池不足百步，一条狭窄曲状的溪流潺潺地流淌着。埠头上三三两两的村民在这里洗菜、洗衣，妇女啪啪地捶衣声打破了村落的宁静。两侧老屋、水榭楼台沿溪一字排开，石桥下植物在风中招摇，这一切使得村落极具水乡气质。溪流是一处经过人工挖掘和改造的水利工程，两侧堤坝和溪底以大块的卵石垒砌，一座座石板桥横跨呈S形流淌的溪流，弯曲的水流有效地减缓水流对堤坝的冲击，弯曲的水流在风水上也是财源滚滚的象征。溪流通过一条条水圳进入村落，利用北高南低的自然地势特征，形成了溪水村边绕，圳水脚下流的场景。水盘活了整座村落，水让山下阳变成一座流动的村落，山下阳成为一座飘荡着浓郁江南水乡情调的传统村落。流动的水系集纳着村落的财气，养真气，荫地气，使得村落生机勃勃，正是水的流动象征着山下阳村的生生不息。

建筑群从月池向四周延伸开去。正前方是庞大的张氏宗祠，后方是张氏香火堂，周围林立着古朴典雅的清代大屋、中西合璧的民国洋楼，那些格调抑扬顿挫的马头墙勾勒出村落嵯峨的历史轮廓，一幢幢或规整或拙朴的建筑中浮现出一派巍峨的气象。

山下阳村的建筑群落类型丰富，最为气势恢宏的当属始建于清嘉庆年间的张氏宗祠，高大规整的宗祠，足以见证了张氏祖上的荣耀与财富。宗祠分为上中下三进厅堂，上堂是祭祀祖先的神圣场所，中堂是族人聚会议事地点，下堂是搭台唱戏的公共场地，上堂横梁上贴满了破碎的学报，前堂横梁上一幅幅彩绘是一出出历史上著名的曲目，让人联想到人生如戏，戏如人生。宗祠多处横梁上施有彩绘，多以民风、民俗等内容为主题，惟妙惟肖，密布着浓郁的历史信息。宗祠同时也是木雕的艺术长廊，各色牛腿、横梁、窗棂雕刻手法细致入微，线条流畅。宗祠以中国红为主色调，在时间的磨砺中色泽渐退，依然透出富丽堂皇的气质。

山下阳村建筑让人惊叹的不是它的形制，更多的是处处飘溢而出的文化气质，门楼、墙体、柱础、窗棂、横梁、雀替上的石雕、砖雕、木雕、绘画、书法美轮美奂，有八仙过海、四君子图、鲤鱼跳龙门、松下问童子、耕种归樵、牡丹芍药图等等，描摹出耕读世家的理想境界。有的干脆将《陋室铭》书写在整片墙体上，色泽如新，仿佛书家刚刚收笔，还飘洒出浓郁的墨香，一转眼已是数百年，让人徒叹光阴斗转。门楣上的石刻或者砖雕的匾额字体隽丽飘逸，多采用典故和传说，有取自《中庸·无忧》中述作，子曰：无忧者，其惟文王乎！以王季为父，以武王为子。父作之，子述之。有取自《书·微子之命》中象贤、崇德，意为殷王元子，惟稽古崇德象贤。有取自《论语·述而》中的窃比非非，意为述而不作，信而好古，窃比于我老彭。更多的是南阳旧家、南山抱翠、南山拱秀、光华丽日、蕴玉怀珠、兰室等等。

围绕着地坛三座大屋的门楣石刻匾额非常讲究，东西对应的两座建筑匾额上分别刻着祥纳启明和瑞映长庚，太白金星在凌晨称作启明星，在夜晚时称作长庚星，意为房子的瑞气映照到了太白金星。面南的西式建筑匾额刻有南极造临，南极仙翁居住的南极星位于南边，它的出现寓意国泰民安，富寿临门。东西北三个方位对应星辰，南面月池代表月亮，正中地坛代表大地。在香火堂大门上有一对并不显眼的对联：塘中有井智水来潮，门外对窗吉星高照。横批：清波映月。明白无误地告诉后人，这是一组星象图！真是让人慨叹山下阳每一组建筑、每一个字眼都埋藏着巨大的玄机。

为了看清整个村落，我爬上了月池右侧一处水泥钢筋结构的红砖楼。站在三楼楼顶向四周眺望，一幅四方神兽拱卫村落的星象图景在眼前徐徐地展开。古人把天空的恒星划分成为三垣和四象七大星区。三垣是紫微垣、太微垣、天市垣，这三垣环绕着北斗七星呈三角状排列。在三垣外围分布着四象：代表东方的青龙，代表西方的白虎，代表南方的朱雀，代表北方的玄武。天上的星宿具体对应到地上，按照坐北朝南的方位排列，故有左青龙、右白虎、前朱雀、后玄武的说法，古人按照这样的方位进行村落选址，象形地貌被称为四大神兽。山下阳村正是按照传统的星象图进行布局的：村后是逶迤起伏的山峦，正中的五阳山仿佛一把巨大的靠背椅，在风水上属于神兽中
sections.content_en:
Shanxiayang: A Star Map Dense with Mysteries

When mentioning feng shui villages, we naturally think of words like magical, hidden, mysterious, and labyrinthine. Shanxiayang Village, located 10 kilometers northwest of Songyang county seat, is exactly such an ancient village full of mechanisms. It is concealed among the many traditional villages in the Songyin River basin, unremarkable, unassuming, not grand, not luxurious. The village closely fits with the natural landscape, everywhere蕴含 the philosophical thought of the unity of heaven and humanity, becoming a classic work of human settlement under the ideal state of the ancients.

Upon entering Shanxiayang Village, a classical mysterious atmosphere drifts over, making one suddenly feel like returning to one's ancestral home. In the village, old houses stand row upon row, alleys wind and twist,悬浮 a vibrant ancient charm. It is a historical painting left behind by modern civilization, allowing one to feel a tranquility and nature beyond the hustle and bustle. Being inside, only with careful observation can one ponder its connotation and unique charm.

Shanxiayang Village superficially presents a rectangular layout, similar to ordinary traditional villages. However, the entire village hides infinite mysteries, creating a giant historical puzzle. Endless alleys divide the village into several kou (mouth)-shaped building clusters. The tall and majestic horse-head walls make the alleys narrow and deep. Buildings are divided into independent yet connected spaces, like a Bagua maze. Dozens of dense cobblestone alleys are like the village's veins, shallow in and deep out, crisscrossing. The cobblestones were screened, basically uniform in size. Over time, the hard and cold cobblestones were polished by footsteps, losing their sharpness, with the road surface glowing with a dark blue luster. There are few crossroads in the village's roads, only countless T-junctions,寓意 that descendants will prosper generation after generation. An alley turns, often leading to the back door of an old house, or a partition wall. After several corners, another passage appears, as if entering a soul-confusing array. These alley gates serve anti-theft and fire-prevention functions; once closed, they isolate the village into independent small spaces, artificially creating separated spaces.

The most stunning building in Shanxiayang Village is the Moon Pool. The Moon Pool injects infinite spiritual energy into the village. In the pool water fall reflections of white walls and black tiles, clearly and brightly revealing all the charm of a water town. Several ducks jump into the pool, quacking, parting the rippling light, breaking a pool of white walls and black tiles. The Moon Pool is the village's landmark and also one of the core buildings of the village's feng shui layout. The Moon Pool lies semicircular in front of the village. The designer, through the feng shui cycle principle that the waning moon will wax again, placed earnest expectations on future generations. A feng shui wall tightly surrounds the Moon Pool, blocking the village's feng shui from flowing out. The Moon Pool never dries up, maintained by the water system surrounding the village. Behind the pool, a well was dug, still clear and incomparable after hundreds of years. According to villagers, there is a living spring at the bottom of the well, with spring water gurgling upward, keeping the well water full. Surprisingly, although the well water and pool water are only a short distance apart, the well water level is 20 centimeters higher than the pool water level. A shirtless man hoists a bucket of fresh water from the old well with a splash, carrying the bucket into a half-open door. This seemingly ordinary well is precisely the ancient village's eyes, witnessing the rise and fall of Shanxiayang Village over 300 years.

Next to the Moon Pool is the square Earth Altar, with stone embankments dividing the Moon Pool and Earth Altar into two. They form a pair of corresponding planar buildings,取意 the sky is round and the earth is square. The Earth Altar is a public activity center; it was the place for sacrificing to heaven and earth, welcoming officials, celebrations, and public gatherings. The Moon Pool and Earth Altar show the Shanxiayang ancestors' reverence for heaven and earth. Here they vividly模拟 the supreme ideal of the unity of heaven and humanity, and standing here we can deeply feel the realm of the unity of heaven, earth, and humanity.

Less than a hundred steps from the Moon Pool, a narrow winding stream flows gurgling. At the dock, villagers in twos and threes wash vegetables and clothes; the women's pattering sound of beating clothes breaks the village's tranquility. Old houses and waterside pavilions on both sides line up along the stream, plants sway in the wind under the stone bridges — all this gives the village a strong water-town quality. The stream is a water conservancy project artificially dug and改造, with both embankments and stream bottom built with large cobblestones. Stone slab bridges span the S-shaped flowing stream; the curved water flow effectively reduces the impact of water on the embankment, and in feng shui, curved water flow also symbolizes rolling wealth. The stream enters the village through一条条 water channels, using the natural terrain feature of high north and low south, forming the scene of stream flowing around the village, channel water flowing underfoot. Water revitalizes the entire village; water makes Shanxiayang a flowing village, and Shanxiayang becomes a traditional village wafting with rich Jiangnan water-town sentiment. The flowing water system gathers the village's wealth, nourishes true energy, shades earth energy, making the village full of vitality. It is precisely the flow of water that symbolizes the endless life of Shanxiayang Village.

The building complex extends outward from the Moon Pool. Directly ahead is the massive Zhang Family Ancestral Hall, behind it is the Zhang Family Incense Hall, surrounded by elegant Qing dynasty great houses and Republic-era Western-style buildings combining Chinese and Western elements. The horse-head walls with varying cadence outline the village's lofty historical silhouette, and a majestic atmosphere emerges from buildings both regular and rustic.

Shanxiayang Village has rich building types. The most imposing is the Zhang Family Ancestral Hall first built during the Qing Jiaqing reign. The tall and regular ancestral hall sufficiently witnesses the glory and wealth of the Zhang ancestors. The ancestral hall is divided into three halls: the upper hall is the sacred place for ancestor worship, the middle hall is the place for clan gatherings and discussions, and the lower hall is the public venue for stage performances. The upper hall's beams are covered with broken academic notices, and the front hall's beams have painted famous historical operas, reminding one that life is like a play, and a play is like life. Many beams of the ancestral hall are painted, mostly themed on folk customs and traditions, vividly depicted, dense with rich historical information. The ancestral hall is also an art gallery of wood carving; various corbels (niutui), beams, and window lattices are exquisitely carved with smooth lines. The ancestral hall uses Chinese red as the main color; although the color has faded under the grinding of time, it still exudes a magnificent temperament.

What amazes people about Shanxiayang's architecture is not its form, but more the cultural气质 overflowing everywhere. Stone carvings, brick carvings, wood carvings, paintings, and calligraphy on gate towers, walls, column bases, window lattices, beams, and sparrow braces are exquisite, including the Eight Immortals Crossing the Sea, the Four Gentlemen Painting, Carp Leaping the Dragon Gate, Asking the Boy Under the Pine, Plowing and Returning with Firewood, Peony and Peony Painting, etc., depicting the ideal realm of a farming-studying family. Some simply write the Inscription of the Humble Room on an entire wall, with color as fresh as if the calligrapher had just finished writing, still wafting rich ink fragrance; in a blink it has been hundreds of years, making one sigh at the passage of time. The stone or brick-carved plaques on door lintels have elegant and飘逸 calligraphy, mostly using allusions and legends: some from the Doctrine of the Mean, No Worries, the Master said: He who has no worries is perhaps King Wen! With King Ji as his father and King Wu as his son. The father made it, the son described it. Some from the Book of Documents, Charge to Weizi, Xiangxian and Chongde, meaning the eldest son of Yin, only examining antiquity and honoring virtue and imitating worthies. Some from the Analects, Shu Er, Qiebi Feifei, meaning transmitting but not creating, believing in and loving antiquity, privately comparing myself to Lao Peng. More are Nanyang Old Family, Nanshan Embracing Green, Nanshan Arching Elegance, Guanghua Beautiful Sun, Yunyu Huaizhu, Orchid Room, etc.

The stone-carved plaques on the door lintels of the three great houses surrounding the Earth Altar are very讲究. The plaques on the two corresponding east-west buildings are respectively carved with Xiangna Qiming (Welcoming the Morning Star) and Ruiying Changgeng (Auspicious Reflection of the Evening Star). Venus is called the Morning Star at dawn and the Evening Star at night, meaning the auspicious energy of the house reflects onto Venus. The south-facing Western-style building's plaque is carved with Nanji Zaolin (South Pole Arrives), the South Pole Immortal lives at the South Star in the south, and its appearance寓意 national peace and prosperity, wealth and longevity. The three directions of east, west, and north correspond to stars; the south Moon Pool represents the moon, and the central Earth Altar represents the earth. On the gate of the Incense Hall, there is an inconspicuous couplet: In the pond there is a well, wise water comes in tide; outside the door facing the window, auspicious stars shine high. Horizontal scroll: Clear Waves Reflect the Moon. It unmistakably tells descendants that this is a star map! It truly makes one sigh that every building group and every word in Shanxiayang hides great mysteries.

To see the entire village clearly, I climbed a red-brick building of reinforced concrete structure on the right side of the Moon Pool. Standing on the third-floor rooftop looking around, a star map picture of four divine beasts guarding the village slowly unfolded before my eyes. The ancients divided the fixed stars in the sky into seven star regions: Three Enclosures and Four Symbols. The Three Enclosures are the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, the Supreme Palace Enclosure, and the Heavenly Market Enclosure; these three enclosures surround the Big Dipper in a triangular arrangement. Around the Three Enclosures are distributed the Four Symbols: the Azure Dragon representing the east, the White Tiger representing the west, the Vermilion Bird representing the south, and the Black Tortoise representing the north. The celestial constellations specifically correspond to the earth, arranged according to the orientation of sitting north and facing south, hence the saying left Azure Dragon, right White Tiger, front Vermilion Bird, back Black Tortoise. The ancients selected village sites according to such orientations, and象形 landforms were called the Four Divine Beasts. Shanxiayang Village is precisely laid out according to the traditional star map: behind the village are winding and undulating mountains, and the central Wuyang Mountain is like a giant armchair, in feng shui belonging to the divine beast...

key_terms.en: Three Enclosures and Four Symbols (Chinese constellations)

sections.name: 吴弄：粉墙黛瓦的建筑长廊
sections.content_zh:
吴弄，粉墙黛瓦的建筑长廊

清中期，一场突如其来的特大洪水将吴弄村夷为平地。这里生活着吴氏家族遭受重创后悲伤地离开了故土，留给历史一个幽暗的背影，也留下了一个空荡荡的村名。那么，吴弄更早的源头在哪儿呢？究竟在什么时候建村？村庄发生过什么样的故事？可惜各种书籍中没有为这个安静的村落遗留下只言片语，村落的喜怒哀乐都被掩埋在了厚厚的土层当中。

清道光四年（1824），叶姓先人叶樟兴在这块被人遗弃的土地上打下第一根木桩，新的吴弄村又开始续写历史。几年后，曾姓先人也相中了吴弄，荒废的土地上飘荡起了袅袅炊烟。叶姓、曾姓依靠农耕、种植烟叶、经商、土地出租逐渐积累下了丰厚的财富，携手成为当地望族。经过几代人的辛勤建设，一座两进五开间的叶氏宗祠、十幢叶姓和两幢曾姓豪宅先后在白地上矗立而起。土改时期，当时仅有230人口的吴弄村，出现了八个半地主，由此可知当时吴弄村的富庶程度。幢幢交接的建筑如同连篇翻开的书页，连片的小青瓦如同码放得整整齐齐的汉字，记载着这座省历史文化名村、中国传统村落欲说还休的历史。

吴弄大屋多为三合院落和四合院落，具有典型的浙派建筑和徽派建筑风格。波浪一样涌动的屋脊将建筑物的几何线条四向扩散，横竖相间的马头墙又将大屋外角一一完整地组合在一起，仿佛榫卯对接，将村庄铆接成一个巨大的整体。这来源于叶姓的一个祖训，家家户户房顶必须连成一片，以显示出叶姓宗族是一个团结和睦的大家庭。

吴弄所有的大屋均是封闭式的庭院建筑，外立面采用夯土墙体，有的是经过抹面的白粉墙，有的裸露着粗粝的黄泥，看似笨重的泥墙在檐瓦的切割下总能够形成各种轻巧的几何形状条。官帽形，翘尾形，直线形，斜角形，夹角形，人字形，圆弧形，飞扬的线条将建筑的轮廓最大限度地拉开，使得大屋挺拔雄阔，建筑呈现出磅礴气势。大屋对外沟通的只有二楼开设的一扇小窗，有方形，有圆形，有八角形，狭小的窗洞起着防盗的作用，也起着通风、采光的作用，小窗印证了古人暗室聚财的传统观念。一个个长方形、正方形的天井在黑漆漆的瓦片当中打开缺口，回形的天井对应天空，应征着四水归堂的风水学说。天井在建筑物内部打通了与天空之间的联系，蓝天、白云在天井中浮现，明亮的光束穿透了重重叠叠的建筑，大屋内部被光照照亮，堂屋通达了，居室敞开了，居住者心中自然开朗。

十多幢单体民居连成一座长方形的巨大建筑，所有的墙体毗接延伸，所有的屋顶连成一片，上千根柱子，100多间房间，32口天井，20多付楼梯，像搭积木一样，从前后左右扩散开去。这种布局引发了我强大的想象，吸引着我进入建筑内部一探究竟。走在建筑内部，隐隐感觉到一股来自历史的推力，它在大屋中无处不在，浮现在村民的脸庞上，停留在建筑的雕刻上，密布建筑的布局上。叶氏族人所有的房子连接在一起，生活在同一片屋檐下，显示出了宗族的团结力和向心力。这是一座以血缘关系和宗族力量凝聚成建筑奇观，浑厚，凝重，饱经风霜，这些建筑来自不同的年代，来自不同的匠人之手，我们却无法辨别它们衔接的痕迹，它们在岁月的磨砺中已经严丝合缝地黏结在了一起。浙南多以宗族为单位的聚居村落，比如大济的吴氏、俞园的俞氏、河阳朱氏、石仓阙氏、杨家堂宋氏等等，但是像吴弄这样整个村落的主体以连环建筑形式出现，这是极其罕见的大手笔。

进入村落，你会发现，一条巷弄中往往会挤着几幢房屋的大门，为了防止风水上的对冲，大门一一相对错开。大屋所有的内门是相通的，迈过一个个天井，走过一座座厅堂，踱过一条条回廊，内部错综复杂，你只要甩开迂回和曲折，沿着直线行走，不知不觉便穿过了整个村落，印证了吴弄村下雨不湿鞋的传说。这些开放通达的建筑可以从中连接任何一家，最大限度地整合了村民生活的一致性，使得他们和谐地生活在一所敞开的大院里，来去自由，相敬如宾，决然没有城市中的冷漠面孔和虚假浮笑。邻里之间的门是敞开的，心也是敞开的，村民之间没有距离，人在这里是亲近的，相处是简单的，生活的细节是自然的。母亲轻声的呼唤从厨房传来，小孩噔噔噔地从楼上跑下来，小黄狗轻吠着从大院外面跑了进来，东家端着碗走进西家，坐在门槛上边吃边聊，一句邻里之间不经意的问候，在老宅某处响起，这一声问候仿佛从百年前传来，至今绕梁不散。

整座吴弄村荡漾在一派浓郁的文化气息当中，精通翰墨的文人留下许多珍贵的文墨，村人美好愿景以笔墨的方式辐射到每一个角落。建筑的门墙上布满了斑驳的壁画，有文房四宝和琴棋书画，有山水人物和花鸟灵兽，有代表四君子的竹菊梅兰，有代表富禄寿禧的如意、梅花鹿、松树、喜鹊。传统知识分子的使命概括在一幅幅吉祥的图案中，体现了先人足够的智慧和笔力。大门门楣上是一方方圣域贤关、泽被南阳、植桂培兰、孕玉怀珠、芝兰翠秀、南山拱秀、南阳草庐、入孝、出悌等石匾额，那些字迹规范着村庄人的言行举止，以儒家经典教化他们知书答礼。特别是宗祠东侧大门上的礼门义路，归纳了吴弄的村落性格，他们在祖先的恩德哺育之下，以礼义为村落的精神，指引他们的日常生活走向秩序化。墙上贴满了癣痕般的学报和发黄的三好学生奖状，精美的牛腿和窗雕依旧被后辈悉心收藏着，吴弄在每一个细小的环节上都标明了这是一个礼仪化的村落。

在村落中，尤以叶氏宗祠、10号、15号、16号、33号大屋最为豪华，保存相对完整。叶氏祠堂建于民国七年（1918），两进，明三暗五开间，一进门厅保留有一座老戏台，依次可以看见叶厚宗祠、保世兹大、叙伦堂三块木牌匾。宗祠正门外石柱上镌刻着一幅对联：丁字剩残碑古碣摩挲怀祖德，卯峰分正派高山仰止挹宗风。对联标明了吴弄叶氏血脉来源于松阳县卯山叶氏。对联没有留下书写者的姓名。内石柱上镌刻着另一幅对联：松栋青来看生意满林定有英才后起，仑溪绿涨溯源头一脉应知世泽长流。楹联为之洞侄女婿、光绪三十年进士林世焘所提写。笔力雄浑，落笔苍远，铿锵有势，一看就是大家手笔。在16号大屋墙上甚至还有王羲之的《兰亭序》，洋洋洒洒，一气呵成，落款：光绪丙午年夏月耐性居士。历史上，欧阳询、虞世南、褚遂良、刘秦妹、赵孟頫、祝允明、文征明、董其昌等人都对《兰亭序》进行摹写，民间更是大规模地对《兰亭序》进行临摹，在建筑物、器物等一切可以书写的地方摹写《兰亭序》。在浩浩荡荡的临摹阵营中，吴弄村的《兰亭序》无疑是民间精品。那些飘飘洒洒的字迹依旧透露出东晋的贵族气息，仿佛只是书家改变，形意并未篡改，一样传递出书者尊贵的姿态。这应该是一名当地学养高深的隐士，

Wunong: An Architectural Corridor of White Walls and Black Tiles

In the mid-Qing dynasty, a sudden catastrophic flood leveled Wunong Village. The Wu family living here, after suffering heavy losses, sadly left their homeland, leaving history a dark背影 and an empty village name. So where was the earlier source of Wunong? When exactly was the village built? What stories happened in the village? Unfortunately, various books left not a single word for this quiet village, and the village's joys and sorrows were all buried in the thick soil.

In the fourth year of Qing Daoguang (1824), Ye family ancestor Ye Zhangxing drove the first wooden stake on this abandoned land, and the new Wunong Village began to continue writing history. A few years later, Zeng family ancestors also took a fancy to Wunong, and curling cooking smoke drifted over the abandoned land. The Ye and Zeng families, through farming, growing tobacco, commerce, and land renting, gradually accumulated rich wealth, joining hands to become local prominent families. After several generations of hard construction, a two-bay five-bay Ye Family Ancestral Hall, ten Ye-family mansions, and two Zeng-family mansions rose one after another on the open land. During the Land Reform period, Wunong Village, with only 230 people at the time, had eight and a half landlords, from which one can know the wealth of Wunong Village at that time. The connected buildings are like pages of a book opened continuously, and the contiguous small gray tiles are like neatly arranged Chinese characters, recording the history of this provincial historical and cultural village and Chinese traditional village that wants to speak but holds back.

Wunong's great houses are mostly three-sided and four-sided courtyard compounds, with typical Zhejiang-style and Huizhou-style architectural features. Wave-like surging ridges spread the geometric lines of the buildings in all directions, and the alternating horse-head walls completely combine the outer corners of the great houses, as if mortise-and-tenon joints对接, riveting the village into a giant whole. This comes from a Ye family ancestral instruction: every household's roof must be connected into one piece, to show that the Ye clan is a united and harmonious big family.

All of Wunong's great houses are enclosed courtyard buildings, with rammed-earth exterior walls. Some are white-plastered walls, some expose coarse yellow mud. The seemingly heavy mud walls, under the cutting of eaves and tiles, can always form various light geometric strips. Official-hat-shaped, upturned-tail-shaped, straight-line, oblique-angle, included-angle, herringbone, arc-shaped — the flying lines maximize the building's outline, making the great houses tall and grand, with the architecture presenting a majestic momentum. The only external communication of the great houses is a small window on the second floor, some square, some round, some octagonal. The narrow window openings serve anti-theft purposes, as well as ventilation and lighting; the small windows confirm the ancients' traditional concept of dark rooms gathering wealth. Rectangular and square courtyards (tianjing) open gaps among the black tiles; the回-shaped courtyards correspond to the sky,应征 the feng shui theory of four waters returning to the hall. The courtyard opens a connection with the sky inside the building; blue sky and white clouds emerge in the courtyard, and bright light beams penetrate the层层叠叠 buildings. The interior of the great house is illuminated, the main hall is accessible, the living rooms are open, and the residents' hearts naturally become cheerful.

More than ten individual residences connect into a giant rectangular building, with all walls adjacent and extending, all roofs connected into one piece, over a thousand columns, over 100 rooms, 32 courtyards, over 20 staircases, like building blocks, spreading from front, back, left, and right. This layout triggered my strong imagination, attracting me to enter the building interior to explore. Walking inside the building, I faintly felt a thrust from history; it is everywhere in the great house, appearing on villagers' faces, resting on the building's carvings, densely distributed in the building's layout. All houses of the Ye clan are connected together, living under the same roof, showing the clan's unity and centripetal force. This is an architectural wonder凝聚 by blood relations and clan power — vigorous, dignified, weathered. These buildings come from different eras and different craftsmen's hands, yet we cannot discern their connection traces; they have been seamlessly bonded together under the grinding of years. Southern Zhejiang has many clan-based聚居 villages, such as the Wu of Daji, the Yu of Yuyuan, the Zhu of Heyang, the Que of Shicang, the Song of Yangjiatang, etc. But like Wunong, where the entire village's主体 appears in the form of connected buildings, this is an extremely rare grand gesture.

Entering the village, you will find that an alley often squeezes the gates of several houses. To prevent feng shui opposition, the gates are staggered one by one. All inner doors of the great houses are connected. Stepping through one courtyard after another, walking through one hall after another, pacing along one corridor after another, the interior is complex. As long as you甩开 detours and twists and walk along a straight line, you will unconsciously pass through the entire village, confirming the legend that in Wunong Village one does not get wet shoes in the rain. These open and accessible buildings can connect any household from within, maximizing the integration of villagers' life consistency, allowing them to live harmoniously in an open courtyard, coming and going freely, respecting each other like guests, absolutely without the cold faces and false smiles of the city. The doors between neighbors are open, and hearts are also open. There is no distance between villagers; people here are close,相处 is simple, and life details are natural. A mother's soft call comes from the kitchen, a child patters down from upstairs, a little yellow dog barks softly and runs in from outside the courtyard, the east household carries a bowl into the west household, sitting on the threshold eating and chatting. A casual greeting between neighbors rings out somewhere in the old house; this greeting seems to come from a hundred years ago, still lingering around the beams.

The entire Wunong Village ripples with a rich cultural atmosphere. Literati proficient in calligraphy left many precious writings, and villagers' beautiful visions radiate to every corner in the form of brush and ink. The door walls of buildings are covered with mottled murals: the four treasures of the study and qin-chess-calligraphy-painting, landscapes and figures, flowers, birds, and spirit beasts; the bamboo, chrysanthemum, plum, and orchid representing the Four Gentlemen; the ruyi, sika deer, pine tree, and magpie representing wealth, status, longevity, and happiness. The mission of traditional intellectuals is summarized in auspicious patterns, reflecting the ancestors' sufficient wisdom and brushwork. On the gate lintels are stone plaques such as Sage Realm and Virtue Gate, Grace Spreads to Nanyang, Planting Cassia and Cultivating Orchids, Nurturing Jade and Embracing Pearls, Orchid and Jade Green Elegance, Nanshan Arching Elegance, Nanyang Thatched Cottage, Entering Filial Piety, Exiting Fraternity. Those characters regulate the villagers' words and deeds, educating them to be learned and courteous through Confucian classics. Especially the Ritual Gate and Righteous Path on the east gate of the ancestral hall summarizes Wunong's village character: nurtured by ancestors' grace, they take ritual and righteousness as the village spirit, guiding their daily life toward order. Walls are covered with moss-like academic notices and yellowed excellent student certificates; exquisite corbels and window carvings are still carefully collected by descendants. Wunong, in every tiny detail, marks that this is a ritualized village.

In the village, the Ye Family Ancestral Hall, and Houses No. 10, 15, 16, and 33 are the most luxurious and relatively well preserved. The Ye Family Ancestral Hall was built in the seventh year of the Republic of China (1918), two bays, with a visible three-bay and hidden five-bay layout. The entrance hall retains an old stage, and one can依次 see three wooden plaques: Ye Hou Ancestral Hall, Preserving the World's Greatness, and Xulun Hall. On the stone pillars outside the main gate of the ancestral hall is engraved a couplet: The Ding character leaves remnant steles and ancient tablets, caressing them cherishes ancestral virtue; from Maofeng branch the orthodox school, looking up to high mountains draws clan style. The couplet indicates that Wunong's Ye family bloodline originates from the Maoshan Ye family of Songyang County. The couplet does not留下 the calligrapher's name. On the inner stone pillars is engraved another couplet: Pine pillars green, seeing abundant life in the forest, surely talented youth will rise; Lunxi green surging, tracing the source to one vein, one knows the family grace flows long. The couplet was written by Lin Shitao, a jinshi of the 30th year of Guangxu and nephew-in-law of Zhi Dong. The brushwork is powerful, the strokes distant and resounding, clearly a master's hand. On the wall of House No. 16, there is even Wang Xizhi's Preface to the Orchid Pavilion, flowing freely in one breath, with the signature: Summer of Guangxu Bingwu year, by the Patient Lay Buddhist. Historically, Ouyang Xun, Yu Shinan, Chu Suiliang, Liu Qinmei, Zhao Mengfu, Zhu Yunming, Wen Zhengming, Dong Qichang and others all copied the Preface to the Orchid Pavilion; among the people, it was copied on a large scale, on buildings, utensils, and一切 writable places. Among the vast copying camp, Wunong Village's Preface to the Orchid Pavilion is undoubtedly a folk masterpiece. Those flowing characters still reveal the aristocratic气息 of the Eastern Jin, as if only the calligrapher changed while the form and meaning were not altered, equally conveying the calligrapher's noble posture. This should be a local hermit of profound learning,

sections.name: 黄家大院：独步浙南的民间宫殿
sections.content_zh:
黄家大院，独步浙南的民间宫殿

1921年的一天，黄家大院的集成堂敞开了大门，这座建设了3年的大屋终于竣工。前来参观的乡人络绎不绝，他们跨进黄家大院，曲径通幽，假山怪石，奇花异草，移步换景，步步风景，在大院中绕行了一大圈才进入集成堂。

这座以以凡事必须集才智和劳作而后大成之而取名的集成堂，的确太让人叹为观止，三进七开间，6个天井，172根柱子，36幅古典故事为主题的木雕，堂内雕梁画栋，回廊、门楣、横梁、牛腿、雀替、斗拱、隔扇、窗格的木雕千姿百态，出神入化，疑为仙手之作。牛腿和雀替上共有204个篆体寿字，据说用遍了汉字篆体中所有的寿字。满堂寿字如同拜寿的童子，他们一起高声祝福屋主黄秋光福如东海，寿比南山。这座立意独到的祝寿堂，因此也称之百寿厅。乡人一路走来，一路暗暗称奇。

108盏大红灯笼高悬在横梁下，红彤彤的色彩将房子映照得如同一座梦幻中的天堂。举目四望，那些在灯光照耀下逐渐温暖起来的构件，浮现出精美的轮廓。客人们好久才回过神来，集成堂上又响起了此起彼伏的赞叹声。

木雕大观园

距离集成堂建成已经过去了90多年，大院也安静了多年，我走进黄家大院的时候，没有一个游客。安静和空旷让大院变得更加的庞大和幽深。

黄家大院历经黄中和、黄绍桂、黄秋光祖孙三代修建而成，同治年间修建的武技厅，光绪年间修建的竹菊轩和梅兰轩，民国十年修建的集成堂，呈三列整齐地排列在大院中，回廊将三列大宅连接在一起。白色的马头墙勾勒出大院巨大的轮廓，高耸的屋脊在空中拉出一道道流畅的几何线条，为大院增添出巍峨的气势。这座占地一万多平方米的大院在动荡和变迁中得以幸存，今天仍以6460平方米的占地面积成为浙西南最大的封闭式古典庄园。我的脑子里接连跳出乔家大院、王家大院、胡雪岩故居、东阳卢宅、诸暨斯宅、莫氏庄园等古建筑群，而眼前的黄家大院也理所当然可以加入到这一串中国著名的民居名录当中。

推开集成堂大门，一个巨大的建筑内部环境豁然出现在面前。一眼就看穿大屋的纵深，穿过门厅、天井、中堂，直达后堂的白粉墙体。一条中轴线将整座建筑一剖为二，大屋严格按照左右对称格局，各个建筑部件经历了近百年的的时光磨砺，刀刻斧凿的痕迹已经蜕化干净，它们出落成了一体建筑，充满了历史的光华和润泽。

在迷宫一样的大院中一间一间地行走，一幢一幢地穿行。那些精致的雕刻首先吸引了我的眼球，文化元素占据在每一个建筑物的细部，我的目光在景致变换中变得如饥似渴。此时，午后的阳光仿佛非常配合我，光线变得柔和起来，给这些构件涂上了一层蜜蜡色泽，包浆变得越发的醇厚，看起来更加充满了历史丰韵感。一个个仙人盘亘于此，或骑仙鹤，或骑凤凰，或骑麒麟，或端坐莲莲，此处俨然成了神仙乐园；一群群书生刻苦攻读，岁寒三友，五子登科，连升三级，金榜题名，这里建筑起读书人理想的天堂；狮子、神鹿、灵猴、玉兔、山羊、金鸡、孔雀、蝙蝠、蜜蜂、蝴蝶等一只只栩栩如生的动物如同刚刚从森林中赶赴而来，在这里召开一场盛大的动物聚会；牡丹、卷草、石榴、松树、竹子、梅花、荷叶等一棵棵花草似乎还带着植物的清香，似乎还在吐纳清凉，这里成了一座天成的植物园；大院太让人意外了，居然将日月、山川、林泉等题材通通搬进了宅第的梁柱上，大有万里江山奔来眼底的磅礴大气。

重重叠叠的雕刻占据了一屋的空间，站在它们面前，主人的雄心壮志和高瞻远瞩已经很清晰地显现出来，它们带着深刻的寓意，在浑然天成中体现出建筑主人的精神指向。黄秋光在雕刻之间寄托自己的理想，巧妙地运用雕刻为家族祈福。整座大院成了自己崇拜的精神图腾：牡丹代表着花开富贵、莲蓬代表着连生百子、五蝠代表着五福临门、竹子代表着高风亮节、马和猴代表着马上封侯、双鹤代表着一品当朝……

在这天地间，有了这么一座黄家大院，是人间的大幸。那么，黄家大院的主人黄秋光是一个怎么样的人呢？我很想在大院中找到黄秋光的雕塑、照片或者画像，可惜什么都没有。我在满眼的木雕中看到了很多人物，有仙人，有官员，有农夫，有樵夫，有渔夫，也有书生，哪一张面孔有着黄秋光的神韵，或者说哪个形象才是黄秋光的真实写照呢？

三分匠人，七分主人。从集成堂的布局和设计来看，黄秋光除了给世人留下财大气粗的形象外，我们的确看到了一个满腹经纶的集大成者。他具备了书画家的潜质，雕刻家的气质，建筑学家的眼力，从建筑设计、木雕出题、选料到审画到入手，均有他的巧妙构思，清楚地阐述了人生观和审美观，完整地呈现出扎实的儒学功底。

最贵的辫子

黄家族谱上记载着祖先如何艰苦创业，如何造福乡梓，如何彪炳千秋，我们其实没有必要去应承。那些对先人习惯性的赞美之词都不足以承载历史，倒是黄家祖先实实在在地给了我们一座看得见的奢华宅第。

黄家三代用了数十年的时间完成了从富商到豪商再到望族的三级跳，黄秋光也成为了地方乡绅的代表人物。黄家到底拥有多少家当呢？鼎盛时期黄家操纵着一个庞大的家族产业，手握一千多亩土地的地契，拥有着众多的地产、房产，在县城黄金路段拥有十余间店面，仅仅一座集成堂就花费了五万五千块大洋！然而，这一切成为黄家家族荣耀的同时，也为黄家在辛亥革命中遭遇的巨大灾难埋下了伏笔。

1912年2月，黄秋光作为省参议员参加了浙江省第一次参议会，在返回处州府（今丽水市）的欢迎晚宴上陷入一场精心策划的圈套，处州军政府都督以黄秋光没有剪辫子为由，将他打入死牢。通知黄家十日内筹集十万大洋赎身，否则立即处死。黄家四处筹钱，几乎贱卖了所有商铺，将田地典当出去，并借了大量的高利贷，东拼西凑才勉强筹集了五万五千块大洋。处州军政分府眼看黄家再也榨不出油水，就没有再坚持当初的要求，释放了黄秋光。

这是民国初年流行
sections.content_en:
Huang Family Compound: The Folk Palace Unmatched in Southern Zhejiang

One day in 1921, the Jicheng Hall of the Huang Family Compound opened its gates. This great house, under construction for 3 years, was finally completed. Villagers came to visit in an endless stream. Stepping into the Huang Family Compound, they found winding paths leading to secluded spots, rockery and strange stones, exotic flowers and rare plants, with changing scenery at every step. They circled a large loop in the compound before entering the Jicheng Hall.

This Jicheng Hall, named for the principle that everything must gather talent and labor before achieving greatness, is truly breathtaking. Three bays, seven openings, 6 courtyards, 172 columns, 36 wood carvings themed on classical stories. Inside the hall, carved beams and painted pillars; the wood carvings on corridors, door lintels, beams, corbels (niutui), sparrow braces (queti), bracket sets (dougong), lattice doors, and window grids are in a thousand poses, superbly executed, seemingly the work of immortals. There are 204 seal-script longevity characters on the corbels and sparrow braces, said to use all longevity characters in Chinese seal script. The hall full of longevity characters is like children paying birthday respects, together loudly blessing the owner Huang Qiuguang with happiness as vast as the Eastern Sea and longevity as high as the Southern Mountain. This uniquely conceived birthday hall is therefore also called the Hundred Longevity Hall. Villagers walked along, secretly marveling all the way.

108 large red lanterns hang high under the beams, their red color illuminating the house like a paradise in a dream. Looking around, those components gradually warming under the lamplight reveal exquisite outlines. Guests took a long time to come to their senses, and waves of赞叹 rose again in the Jicheng Hall.

Wood Carving Grand View Garden

More than 90 years have passed since the Jicheng Hall was completed, and the compound has been quiet for many years. When I entered the Huang Family Compound, there was not a single tourist. The quietness and emptiness made the compound even more vast and profound.

The Huang Family Compound was built over three generations by Huang Zhonghe, Huang Shaogui, and Huang Qiuguang. The Martial Arts Hall built during the Tongzhi reign, the Bamboo-Chrysanthemum Studio and Plum-Orchid Studio built during the Guangxu reign, and the Jicheng Hall built in the tenth year of the Republic of China, are arranged neatly in three rows within the compound, with corridors connecting the three rows of great houses. White horse-head walls outline the compound's giant silhouette, and the high ridges draw smooth geometric lines in the air, adding a majestic momentum to the compound. This compound, covering over 10,000 square meters, survived turmoil and changes, and today still covers 6,460 square meters, making it the largest enclosed classical manor in southwestern Zhejiang. In my mind, names like the Qiao Family Compound, Wang Family Compound, Hu Xueyan Former Residence, Dongyang Lu Residence, Zhuji Si Residence, and Mo Family Manor popped up one after another, and the Huang Family Compound before me can naturally join this list of famous Chinese residences.

Pushing open the gate of the Jicheng Hall, a vast interior architectural environment suddenly appeared before me. One can see through the depth of the great house at a glance, passing through the entrance hall, courtyard, central hall, straight to the white-plastered wall of the rear hall. A central axis divides the entire building into two halves; the great house strictly follows a left-right symmetrical layout. Each building component, after nearly a hundred years of time's grinding, has shed all traces of chisel and axe, maturing into an integrated building full of historical luster and moisture.

Walking room by room, passing through building after building in the maze-like compound. Those exquisite carvings first caught my eye; cultural elements occupy every detail of the building, and my gaze became insatiable as the scenery changed. At this moment, the afternoon sunlight seemed to cooperate perfectly with me, the light becoming soft, coating these components with a beeswax luster, the patina becoming increasingly mellow, looking even more full of historical charm. Immortals dwell here, riding cranes, phoenixes, or qilin, or sitting on lotus platforms — this place has become a fairy paradise; groups of scholars study diligently, the Three Friends of Winter, five sons passing exams, three consecutive promotions, passing the imperial examination — here is built the ideal paradise of scholars; lions, divine deer, spirit monkeys, jade rabbits, goats, golden roosters, peacocks, bats, bees, butterflies and other lifelike animals seem to have just arrived from the forest, holding a grand animal gathering here; peonies, scrolling grass, pomegranates, pine trees, bamboo, plum blossoms, lotus leaves and other flowers and plants seem to still carry plant fragrance, still breathing coolness — here has become a natural botanical garden; the compound is most surprising, actually bringing themes of sun, moon, mountains, rivers, forests and springs onto the beams and columns of the residence, with the grand momentum of ten thousand miles of rivers and mountains coming into view.

Layers upon layers of carvings occupy the space of an entire room. Standing before them, the owner's ambitions and foresight are clearly显现; they carry profound meanings, naturally reflecting the building owner's spiritual direction. Huang Qiugang placed his ideals among the carvings, skillfully using carvings to bless the family. The entire compound became his worshiped spiritual totem: peonies represent blossoming wealth and honor, lotus pods represent continuous birth of many sons, five bats represent five blessings arriving, bamboo represents noble character, horse and monkey represent immediate enfeoffment, double cranes represent top-ranking official...

In this world, having such a Huang Family Compound is a great blessing for humanity. So, what kind of person was Huang Qiuguang, the owner of the Huang Family Compound? I very much wanted to find a sculpture, photo, or portrait of Huang Qiuguang in the compound, but unfortunately there was nothing. In the wood carvings filling my eyes, I saw many figures: immortals, officials, farmers, woodcutters, fishermen, and scholars. Which face has Huang Qiuguang's charm, or which image is Huang Qiuguang's true portrayal?

Three parts craftsman, seven parts master. From the layout and design of the Jicheng Hall, besides leaving the world an image of great wealth, Huang Qiuguang indeed showed himself to be a learned synthesizer. He possessed the potential of a calligrapher-painter, the temperament of a sculptor, and the eye of an architect. From architectural design, wood carving themes, material selection, painting review to execution, all had his ingenious conception, clearly阐述 his outlook on life and aesthetics, completely presenting a solid foundation in Confucian learning.

The Most Expensive Braid

The Huang family genealogy records how the ancestors worked hard to start a business, how they benefited the hometown, and how they left a glorious legacy. We actually have no need to accept all of this. Those habitual words of praise for ancestors are not enough to carry history; rather, the Huang ancestors实实在在 gave us a visible luxurious residence.

The Huang family used decades to complete a three-level jump from wealthy merchant to grand merchant to prominent family, and Huang Qiuguang also became a representative figure of local gentry. How much property did the Huang family actually own? At its peak, the Huang family controlled a vast family enterprise, holding land deeds for over 1,000 mu of land, owning numerous properties and real estate, and over ten shops in the county's golden section. Just one Jicheng Hall cost 55,000 silver dollars! However, while all this became the glory of the Huang family, it also laid the groundwork for the great disaster the Huang family遭遇 during the Xinhai Revolution.

In February 1912, Huang Qiuguang, as a provincial senator, attended the first provincial council of Zhejiang Province. At a welcome banquet on his return to Chuzhou Prefecture (today's Lishui City), he fell into a carefully plotted trap. The military government governor of Chuzhou, on the grounds that Huang Qiuguang had not cut his braid, threw him into death row. He notified the Huang family to raise 100,000 silver dollars for ransom within ten days, otherwise he would be immediately executed. The Huang family raised money everywhere, almost selling all shops at low prices, pawning farmland, and borrowing large amounts of high-interest loans, scraping together barely 55,000 silver dollars. Seeing that the Huang family could no longer be squeezed, the Chuzhou military government branch did not insist on the original demand and released Huang Qiuguang.

This was a popular practice in the early Republic of China...

sections.name: 西屏：凝固的建筑秘籍
sections.content_zh:
西屏，凝固的建筑秘籍

每次经过西屏车站，我总会情不自禁地仰望钟楼，巨大的指针一动不动地指向上午9点，它已经静止了十多年。时间不愿意为这座城市走动，钟声也不再为这座城市敲响。我深深地怀疑，这座建于唐贞元年间（785—805）的西屏镇，似乎也已经随着指针停顿了下来，成为一只停摆的钟。

事实上，这座有着1200年历史的古城的确停顿了下来，大量的古建筑停顿在了自己的年份上。以人民大街为中轴，一平方多公里的古城及周边分布着北宋古塔、南宋古井、元代堰渠、明代牌坊、明清老宅、清代庙宇、民国骑楼……徜徉其间，举目历史，不知今昔是何年的感觉悄然涌上心头。

诸多古建筑勾勒出这座省级历史文化名城的轮廓，西屏镇已然成为浙江省目前保留面积最大、现存商业业态最完整的古县城。绵延的建筑仿佛一部叙述体的长卷本，小城俨然又成为一本古建筑秘籍。

一座被钉住的古城

在西屏老城行走，你会发现主要老街鲜有十字路，大多为丁字街。人民大街与横街交汇、人民大街与市堪头交汇、济川路猪行路交汇、塔头街与猪行路交汇、塔头街与桥亭街交汇、荷田岭路与猪行路交汇、南直街与市堪头交汇、官儒路与官塘门交汇……一条接着一条丁字街跳到眼前。曾经的十字路也在拆迁中被截断，成为一个名不副实的地名。

奇特的格局让人不禁想起了中国两个以丁字街格局而著名的古城。一个是北京，北京内城紫禁城外还套着一座外城，在没有开通长安街之前，道路延伸到了城市中央的紫禁城下，自然形成断头路，也就是丁字街；另一个就是太原，历史上太原王气太重，成为唐王朝的龙兴之地，也出了不少割据势力。为了钉死王气，所以在太原留下了大量的丁字街。西屏丁字街的格局是如何形成的呢？是先人特意设计还是偶然所为？一次次在西屏行走，我突然想到了紧紧挨着古城的松阴溪。历史上，西屏屡遭水患，讲究风水的古人设计出丁字街格局，希望把古城钉在原位，避免水患的侵袭。即使在发大水之时，洪水沿着曲折的街道涌入城区，丁字街也能够有效地减缓洪流，从而保护住核心城区免受冲击。由于西屏坐落在平原，除了西面横着低矮的西屏山、吴家山之外，三面空荡荡。聪明的先人以丁字街将城市巧妙地围成一个藏的格局，南北和东西对向的风无法贯穿整个城区，使得居民在冬天不必遭受凛冽的西北风侵袭。

非常有意思，在南直街南端坐落着一座丁氏宗祠，让人想起绩溪龙川村的格局，村尾处坐落着一户丁姓人家，如同一只丁字形的船锚稳住船形古村龙川。我查阅了相关资料，发现这只是一个巧合，却留给了后人无数的想象。

千岁延庆寺塔

只恐云霄有路通，层层登处接星宫。洗花寒滴翠檐雨，惊梦夜摇金铎风。僧老不离青嶂里，樵声多在白云中。相逢尽说从天降；七宝休夸是鬼工。（《延庆寺塔》）

宋代诗人朱琳所写的延庆寺塔位于城西3公里处。楼阁式砖木结构，六面七级，高38.32米，从远处仰看，四周挑角飞檐，塔顶安放着铁铸圆盘轮，塔檐自下而上逐级缩小，延庆寺塔微微倾斜地矗立在云龙山顶。塔檐翘角上挂铁铃，轻风吹过，叮叮当当的铃声在空气中传播，带来了悦耳的佛音。据《松阳县志》记载，太平兴国四年（公元979年），行达禅师奉旨西行，到中印度，得《大经论》八部舍利四十九粒以归。受到朝廷嘉赐，为此发愿建塔，以藏舍利。经多方筹募，于咸平二年（公元999年）动工，到咸平五年（公元1002年）建成。这座塔历经千年风雨飘摇依旧傲然挺立，成了江南诸塔中保存最完整的北宋原物。1156年，杭州六和塔完成重建，它比延庆寺塔还晚了154年。延庆寺塔如同古城的一个时间刻度，定格在了公元1002年。登上塔芯黝黑的楼梯，我们仿佛进行了一场穿越，轻而易举地返回到北宋年间。我无数次地登临此塔，一次，偶然抚摩到了砖块上凸出的汉字，一个楷书的吉，围着塔身细细查找，居然有数十个吉字密布塔身。记得南京明代城墙上许多城砖都有铭文，刻着造砖工匠的籍贯姓名，那是保质证明，在法律上叫勒刻工名。这些吉字具有同样的功能，说明在北宋的时候就有质量追踪制度，一旦日后砖块出现质量问题，吉字号窑商就将承担法律责任。千年前建塔工匠的手模和我的手不期而遇，手手吻合着，那是一群什么模样的工匠呢？他们在吉字号窑商的带领下，烧造出这些逾千年而依旧完整结实的砖块，这座塔延续着这些建塔者生命，成了凝聚他们智慧、力量、信誉和信仰的丰碑。

延庆寺塔西侧是一处长约百米的碑林，几十块各个时代的石碑嵌在长廊的墙体中。文字经过风雨剥蚀已经漫漶得无法辨识，我只能抚摸石碑上的字迹，肌肤的机敏可以感触到笔法的遒劲和舒缓，不同时代的文字经过手的抚摸渐渐抵达内心，此时的文字在我心中排列得整整齐齐，文字的力量变得举重若轻。我想，这该是历史给予我的点拨吧。

兄弟进士牌坊

西屏曾经坐落过8座牌坊，如今仅存一座兄弟进士牌坊和一座贞节牌坊，位于下马街的兄弟进士牌坊已成为省内牌坊建筑的经典。明成化二年詹雨考中丙戌科进士，后官至广东左参政，素有政绩，深受百姓称道。明弘治九年，胞弟詹宝考中丙辰科进士，授予新昌县令。乡人于明弘治
sections.content_en:
Xiping: The Frozen Architectural Secret Manual

Every time I pass Xiping Station, I can't help but look up at the clock tower. The giant hands motionlessly point to 9 AM, having been stationary for over ten years. Time is unwilling to move for this city, and the bell no longer rings for it. I deeply suspect that Xiping Town, built during the Tang Zhenyuan reign (785-805), seems to have also stopped along with the clock hands, becoming a stopped clock.

In fact, this ancient city with 1,200 years of history has indeed stopped, with a large number of ancient buildings frozen in their own eras. With Renmin Street as the central axis, the ancient city of over one square kilometer and its surroundings feature Northern Song ancient pagodas, Southern Song ancient wells, Yuan dynasty weirs and canals, Ming dynasty archways, Ming-Qing old houses, Qing dynasty temples, and Republic-era arcade buildings... Wandering among them, history meets the eye everywhere, and a feeling of not knowing what year it is quietly surges in the heart.

Numerous ancient buildings outline the silhouette of this provincial historical and cultural city. Xiping Town has already become the ancient county seat with the largest preserved area and most complete existing commercial formats in Zhejiang Province today. The continuous buildings are like a narrative long scroll, and the small town has become an architectural secret manual.

A City Nailed in Place

Walking in old Xiping, you will find that the main old streets rarely have crossroads; most are T-junctions. Renmin Street intersects with Heng Street, Renmin Street intersects with Shikan Tou, Jichuan Road intersects with Zhuxing Road, Tatou Street intersects with Zhuxing Road, Tatou Street intersects with Qiaoting Street, Hetianling Road intersects with Zhuxing Road, Nanzhi Street intersects with Shikan Tou, Guanru Road intersects with Guantang Gate... T-junction after T-junction jumps before the eyes. The former crossroads were also截断 during demolition, becoming a name that does not match reality.

The peculiar pattern reminds one of two ancient Chinese cities famous for their T-junction layout. One is Beijing: inside Beijing's inner city, the Forbidden City is wrapped by an outer city. Before Chang'an Avenue was opened, roads extended to the Forbidden City at the city center, naturally forming dead-end roads, i.e., T-junctions. The other is Taiyuan: historically Taiyuan had too much royal qi, becoming the dragon-rising place of the Tang dynasty and producing many separatist forces. To nail down the royal qi, many T-junctions were left in Taiyuan. How did Xiping's T-junction pattern form? Was it deliberately designed by ancestors or accidental? Walking in Xiping again and again, I suddenly thought of the Songyin River紧挨着 the ancient city. Historically, Xiping suffered repeated floods. The feng-shui-conscious ancients designed the T-junction pattern, hoping to nail the ancient city in place and avoid flood侵袭. Even during major floods, as floodwater surged into the city along winding streets, the T-junctions could effectively slow the torrent, thereby protecting the core urban area from impact. Since Xiping sits on a plain, except for the low Xiping Mountain and Wu Mountain to the west, three sides are empty. The clever ancestors used T-junctions to巧妙ly enclose the city in a hidden pattern, so that north-south and east-west opposing winds could not penetrate the entire urban area, sparing residents from the biting northwest wind in winter.

Interestingly, at the southern end of Nanzhi Street stands a Ding Family Ancestral Hall, reminding one of the layout of Jixi Longchuan Village, where a household with the Ding surname sits at the village tail, like a T-shaped anchor stabilizing the boat-shaped ancient village Longchuan. I查阅 related materials and found this is just a coincidence, yet it leaves后人 countless imagination.

Thousand-Year Yanqing Temple Pagoda

Only fearing that clouds have a road to heaven, climbing layer by layer connects to the star palace. Washing flowers, cold drips from green eaves; startling dreams, night shakes golden bell wind. Old monks never leave the green peaks; woodcutter sounds are mostly in white clouds. Meeting, all say descended from heaven; seven treasures need not praise as ghost work. (Yanqing Temple Pagoda)

The Yanqing Temple Pagoda, written about by Song dynasty poet Zhu Lin, is located 3 kilometers west of the city. A pavilion-style brick-wood structure, six-sided, seven levels, 38.32 meters high. Viewed from afar, with upturned eaves on all sides, the top holds an iron-cast disc wheel, and the eaves gradually缩小 from bottom to top. The Yanqing Temple Pagoda stands slightly tilted on Yunlong Mountain. Iron bells hang at the upturned eave corners; when the breeze blows, the ding-ding-dang-dang bell sounds spread in the air, bringing pleasant Buddhist sounds. According to the Songyang County Gazetteer, in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo (979 AD), Master Xingda, by imperial order, traveled west to Central India, returning with eight parts of the Great Sutra and 49 śarīra (relics). Receiving imperial reward, he vowed to build a pagoda to house the relics. After extensive fundraising, construction began in the second year of Xianping (999 AD) and was completed in the fifth year of Xianping (1002 AD). This pagoda, after a thousand years of wind and rain, still stands proudly, becoming the most completely preserved Northern Song original among pagodas in Jiangnan. In 1156, the Liuhe Pagoda in Hangzhou completed reconstruction, 154 years later than the Yanqing Temple Pagoda. The Yanqing Temple Pagoda is like a time marker of the ancient city, frozen at 1002 AD. Climbing the dark stairs in the pagoda core, we seem to travel through time, easily returning to the Northern Song dynasty. I have climbed this pagoda countless times. Once, I偶然 touched raised Chinese characters on a brick — a regular-script ji (auspicious). Carefully searching around the pagoda body, I found dozens of ji characters densely covering the pagoda. I remember that many city bricks on Nanjing's Ming dynasty city walls have inscriptions, carving the brickmakers' native places and names — that is a quality guarantee, legally called leke gongming (inscribing worker names). These ji characters have the same function, indicating that in the Northern Song there was already a quality tracking system: if bricks later had quality problems, the ji-marked kiln merchants would bear legal responsibility. The handprints of pagoda builders from a thousand years ago met my hand unexpectedly, hand to hand. What did those craftsmen look like? Under the leadership of the ji-marked kiln merchants, they fired bricks that remain complete and solid after over a thousand years. This pagoda延续s these builders' lives, becoming a monument凝聚 their wisdom, strength, reputation, and faith.

West of the Yanqing Temple Pagoda is a stele forest about 100 meters long, with dozens of stone steles from various eras embedded in the corridor walls. The文字, eroded by wind and rain, has become too blurred to read. I can only stroke the characters on the steles; the sensitivity of my skin can feel the powerful and relaxed brushwork. Characters from different eras, through the touch of hand, gradually reach the heart. At this moment, the characters arrange themselves neatly in my mind, and the power of文字 becomes举重若轻. I think this must be the enlightenment history gives me.

Brothers Jinshi Archway

Xiping once had 8 archways, but now only one Brothers Jinshi Archway and one Chastity Archway remain. The Brothers Jinshi Archway on Xiama Street has become a classic of archway architecture in the province. In the second year of Ming Chenghua, Zhan Yu passed the Bingxu imperial examination as jinshi, later serving as Guangdong Left Assistant Administration Commissioner, with notable achievements and praised by the people. In the ninth year of Ming Hongzhi, his younger brother Zhan Bao passed the Bingchen imperial examination as jinshi, appointed as magistrate of Xinchang County. Villagers, in Ming Hongzhi...
