Afterword

Feng Jicai pointed out in The Dilemma and Way Out of Traditional Villages: At the beginning of the 21st century, the total number of natural villages in China was 3.63 million. By 2010, just ten years later, the total had sharply dropped to 2.71 million. In ten years, 900,000 natural villages disappeared. For our traditional agricultural country, this is an earth-shattering number.

After Zhejiang entered industrial civilization, traditional villages rapidly disappeared, and there are few traditional villages left in industrialized areas. Songyang County has become one of the last gathering places of traditional villages in Zhejiang. To some extent, Songyang County bears the heavy responsibility of protecting Zhejiang's traditional village culture. However, the protection status of traditional villages in Songyang County is also not optimistic.

Just like the fate of traditional villages across the country, some ancient buildings have been severely damaged by lightning strikes, floods, fires, and insects; some uninhabited old houses are in a state of abandonment. Under industrial encroachment, new rural construction, and old village renovation, a batch of traditional villages are being destroyed. The urbanization process has caused rural folk culture to gradually disappear, and some ancient buildings in urgent need of repair have entered the dangerous building list due to lack of maintenance funds. The ecological chain of these traditional villages, which凝聚 the essence of 1,800 years of agricultural civilization history, is already very fragile. Without protection, they may completely disappear from sight in a few decades.

In recent years, the value of traditional villages in Songyang County has gradually been recognized and valued by the people and the government. A group of folk custom enthusiasts, based in Songyang, spontaneously formed a民间 traditional village protection group. They use文字 and cameras to record the cultural relics of traditional villages — architecture, clans, farming-studying, commerce, religion, feng shui, customs, etc. They have excavated, collected, and organized written materials on over 100 traditional villages, photographed over 300 villages, and published multiple books such as Village Records and Songgu Village Language, laying the foundation for the protection, development, and utilization of traditional villages. Currently, traditional village protection has been included in the cultural strategy of the Songyang County Party Committee and Government, with the slogan Ancient Village Revival proposed, and protection plans and measures formulated. Forty-four protected villages have been designated, and restoration actions for some traditional villages such as Shicang Seven Villages, Jieshou, and Shanxiayang have been launched. Of the county's over 230 ancestral halls, over 70 have been repaired. The County Local Records Office has collected over 600 genealogies, organizing some family laws, family trees, and village rules and agreements. They propose cultivating traditional virtues such as gentleness, kindness, respect, frugality, and yielding, and self-restraint and return to ritual; protecting folk customs such as production, life, festivals, and markets; and protecting cultural resources such as folk drama, sacrifices, beliefs, and various handicrafts. These substantive actions mark an important step in the protection of traditional villages in Songyang County, which has exploratory significance for protecting the cultural history and architectural history of southwestern Zhejiang. With the joint efforts of all sectors of society, the protection of traditional villages in Songyang County, which was originally in a dilemma, may move toward spring.

This book Jiangnan Secret Realm: Songyang Traditional Villages, edited by the Songyang County Federation of Literary and Art Circles and published by the China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Publishing House, presents part of the cultural heritage of Songyang's traditional villages to readers in the form of cultural essays, with village visits as the main line, richly illustrated with text and photos. However, Songyang's traditional villages are splendid and colorful, and what we have written and photographed is only a tiny part of the essence. We hope that, guided by the text and photos in the book, you will never tire of the beautiful landscapes along the way and the endless rural culture. What we期待 is not the noisy tourism of glancing at flowers while riding a horse, but clearly finding your spiritual home among these ancient mud walls, bricks and tiles, stone carvings, wood carvings, folk customs, and local products. We hope that the charm of these traditional villages can comfort a lost and confused urban soul...

I wrote this book intermittently over many years in my spare time. Due to my limited scholarship, vision, and historical perspective, this book inevitably contains omissions and subjective assumptions; I hope readers will correct them. During the writing process, I received help from local cultural and historical experts such as Tang Guangxin, Ye Rongliang, Ye Yongxuan, Ye Jianhong, and Ye Ping, and included photos by local photographers such as Ye Gaoxing, Mao Jinjun, Zheng Zhongmin, Que Xianrong, and Wu Jun. I thank them all here!

Lu Xiaomin
November 2013, in Songyang
